newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Tax changes encourage Dutch capital flight - paper.
newsitem.headline: Tax changes encourage Dutch capital flight - paper.

text.p: A record 50 billion guilders of Dutch capital has left the country this year for Belgium ahead of tougher tax laws effective from January 1, newspaper NRC Handelsblad said on Saturday.
The paper, quoting tax experts, said that in 1996 around 2,500 wealthy Dutch residents moved to Belgium, a five-fold increase on previous years.
This will result in a loss of a billion guilders annually to the Dutch state, the paper said.
The scale of the exodus, if true, would be a blow to the government which had predicted that the tighter tax regime would only double the flow of capital overseas.
One tax expert the paper quoted said the outflow would be five to ten times its normal level.
From the New Year, Dutch residents with five percent or more of a company's shares will be subject to a 25 percent duty if and when they cash in their shares.

The government is closing a loop-hole in the system which has allowed directors and major equity-holders to receive no income, but to live off their share capital and claim subsidies intended for lower income groups.
